predecessors.name: Kingdom of Arles
predecessors.text: Otto-William's 'domains in northern parts of the Burgundian realm'; the page puts the county in 'Upper Burgundy and the Kingdom of Arles'

successors.name: Duchy of Burgundy
successors.text: Franche-Comté and Artois, with Flanders, Nevers and Rethel, inherited by Margaret III and Philip the Bold in 1384

ledger.x: 982: Count Otto-William forms the County of Burgundy.
1329: Artois passes to the Countess of Burgundy.
1330: Joan III marries Odo IV, Duke of Burgundy; the county passes with Artois to the house of the dukes.
21 November 1361: Philip of Rouvres dies and the county leaves the ducal house.
1366: the name Free County of Burgundy becomes official.
1382: Margaret I bequeaths the county to her son Louis II of Flanders.
1384: the county passes to Margaret III and Philip the Bold and joins the Burgundian lands.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line of the county is dated on the five pages opened; its limits (Besançon, Salins, Montbéliard, Belfort) are not given, and Artois is drawn as the Cliopatria Artois shape.
